ops.title: task build rewrites the tracked plugin/bin/ccx symlink, so any unscoped ship commits it
ops.description:
`Taskfile.yml:35` runs `ln -sf ../../bin/ccx plugin/bin/ccx` as part of `task build`. `plugin/bin/ccx` is tracked, and its committed value is `../scripts/install-binary.sh`, so every build leaves the working copy dirty on a tracked file that must never be committed: landing the flipped symlink would repoint the plugin's install path at the builder's local `bin/ccx` for every consumer.

Today this is only survivable because ship's path scoping lets a commit exclude it, and because whoever is shipping happens to notice. An unscoped `ccx vcs ship -m "..."` in this repo silently commits the flip.

Found while shipping the path-scoped ship fix (0.57.0): `git status` showed ` M plugin/bin/ccx` after the implementer ran `task build`.

Options worth weighing: untrack it and generate it (it is a build artifact wearing a tracked file's clothes); point the build at a gitignored path instead; or have the build restore the committed target on exit.

ops.text: task build leaves plugin/bin/ccx clean in git status, or the file is no longer tracked
A plain unscoped ccx vcs ship in this repo cannot commit a local-build symlink flip
